KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                Page 1 of 9
 KEVIN KENNEDY’S MOTION TO THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS
                                  FOR RECONSIDERATION OF THE
       OCTOBER 13, 2026, BALLOT MEMORANDUM AND, IN THE ALTERNATIVE,
                                    MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION


                                            I. INTRODUCTION

           Pro se intervenor and retired professional engineer Kevin Kennedy (“Mr. Kennedy”)

moves for reconsideration of the Commission’s October 13, 2026, Ballot Memorandum under 16

Tex. Admin. Code (“TAC”) § 22.123(b). In the alternative, he moves for clarification of its legal

effect. 1 The Ballot Memorandum states, in its entirety:

                   The Commission voted to not add the Interim Appeal of SOAH
                   Order No. 35 to any open meeting agenda. 2

           Mr. Kennedy asks the Commission to reconsider the “deemed dismissal” of the Appeal

and/or provide a statement clarifying exactly what the October 13 vote decided.


                                      II. PROCEDURAL HISTORY

           On September 20, 2026, Mr. Kennedy moved the ALJs to order an independent technical

investigation and forensic audit of the ERCOT modeling used in the PBRP. 3 On September 22,

2026, SOAH Order No. 35 denied the Motion. The ALJs order did not address the merits. It stated:

“SOAH ALJs do not possess self-initiating regulatory or investigative power.” 4 In a footnote, the




1
 Ballot Memorandum (Oct. 13, 2026) (Item No. 6642 in Docket No. 59475). Mr. Kennedy’s appeal was filed in
both Docket No. 59182 (Item No. 619) and Docket No. 59475 (Item No. 6601), and this motion is filed in both
dockets for that reason.
2
    59475, Item No. 6642 at 1.
3
  Kevin Kennedy’s Motion for an Independent Technical Investigation and Forensic Audit (Sept. 20, 2026) (59475,
Item No. 6589).
4
    SOAH Order No. 35 at 3 (Sept. 22, 2026) (59475, Item No. 6597).



KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                               Page 2 of 9
 ALJs identified where that authority resides: “Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act, the

Commission has complete oversight and exclusive jurisdiction over ERCOT.” 5

           On September 23, 2026, Mr. Kennedy filed his Appeal of SOAH Order No. 35 and Request

for Commission-Directed Independent Technical Investigation and Forensic Audit. 6 That pleading

asked for two distinct things: that the Commission grant the appeal of SOAH Order No. 35, and

that the Commission exercise its own authority under PURA § 39.151(d) and (d-4) to direct an

independent technical investigation.7 Applicants responded on September 30, 2026. 8 The Ballot

Memorandum issued on October 13, 2026.


                             III. TIMELINESS AND PROCEDURAL BASIS

           Subsection 22.123(b)(1) provides that motions for reconsideration “are available for any

interim order of the commission that immediately prejudices a substantial or material right of a

party or materially affects the course of the hearing.”9 A motion must be filed within five working

days from the date the written interim order is filed.10 The Ballot Memorandum was filed on

Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Five working days from that date is Tuesday, October 20, 2026. This

motion is timely.

           Mr. Kennedy recognizes that the rules provide for an appeal to be “deemed denied” if no

commissioner places it on an open meeting agenda within 20 days, and that no statement of reasons

is required for a deemed denial.11 If the Ballot Memorandum is only the notice that subsection

6
    59475, Item No. 6601.

8
    Applicants’ Response to Kevin Kennedy’s Appeal of SOAH Order No. 35 (Sept. 30, 2026) (Item No. 6610).
9

11

KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                                  Page 3 of 9
 (a)(6) requires, and not an interim order of the Commission, subsection (b) may not apply. In that

event, Mr. Kennedy asks the Commission to treat this filing as a motion for clarification.


                                       IV. GROUNDS FOR RELIEF

A.         No decisionmaker has ruled on the request addressed to the Commission’s own
           authority.

           SOAH Order No. 35 made no finding that the PBRP model was valid, nor did it find that

the requested investigation was unnecessary. It denied the Motion because SOAH ALJs lack self-

initiating investigative power, and it identified the Commission as the body with jurisdiction over

ERCOT. PURA confirms that allocation. The Commission “has complete authority to oversee and

investigate the independent organization’s finances, budget, and operations as necessary to ensure

the organization’s accountability and to ensure that the organization adequately performs the

organization’s functions and duties.”12 The Commission may also “conduct audits of an

independent organization’s performance of the functions prescribed by this section.” 13

           Intertwined and supportive of Mr. Kennedy’s appeal for the need to audit ERCOT’s

“engineering” practices, is the issue of sealing engineering work by a professional engineer, as

required by the Texas Engineering Practice Act (“TEPA”). The ERCOT engineering reports in

this evidentiary record do not bear the required seal of a professional engineer. 14 ERCOT has not

shown itself to be licensed to practice engineering in the State of Texas. 15 The Permian Basin

Reliability Plan, 2024 Regional Transmission Plan (“RTP”), and the 2025 RTP may not be

accepted and utilized by the Commission due to the lack of sealing and engineering accountability,




12
     PURA § 39.151(d).
13
     PURA § 39.151(d-4)(3).
14
     Intervenor Tom Green’s Reply Brief on Remand at 15 (October 19, 2026) (59475, Item No. 6645).
15
     Intervenor Tom Green’s Reply Brief on Remand at 14-15 (October 19, 2026) (59475, Item No. 6645).



KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                                  Page 4 of 9
 as stipulated by TEPA. 16 The Commission, and in particular Commission Jackson, P.E., has a

statutory duty to report ERCOT’s violation of TEPA to the Texas Board of Professional Engineers

(“TBPELS”) for investigation and possible disciplinary action. 17

           ERCOT’s apparent failure to comply with State statutes, and the Commission’s duty to

reject the ERCOT studies and report that failing to TBPELS, are part and parcel to Mr. Kennedy’s

request for a technical investigation and forensic audit of ERCOT’s engineering practices. The

Commission has both the authority and the duty to act in compliance with State statutes and their

own rules, as well as in the best interest of the public. If the Commission chooses not to grant Mr.

Kennedy’s Appeal, they must explain why, for the record.

           That authority is discretionary. Section 39.151(d-4) says the Commission “may” conduct

audits, and Mr. Kennedy acknowledged as much in his appeal. 18 As such, Mr. Kennedy’s request

here is narrow. A request addressed to a discretionary power calls for an exercise of that discretion,

and the record does not presently show whether the Commission exercised that power. The

October 13 vote may have addressed only whether to schedule the appeal of SOAH Order No. 35.

           The Commission may direct ERCOT to take an official action only through “a contested

case,” “rulemaking,” or “a memorandum or written order adopted by a majority vote.” 19 The

Legislature also directed the Commission to adopt rules requiring “that proposed commission

directives be included as an item on a commission meeting agenda” with an opportunity for public

comment. 20 The Ballot Memorandum reflects only that the Appeal was not placed on an agenda.

 If that means the Commission has not yet decided whether to exercise its PURA § 39.151 authority,

then the Commission should state Item No. 6601 has not been ruled on.

B.         A deemed denial is not a merits ruling, but a ballot memoranda has been cited as
           such.

           On June 22, 2026, the Commission issued a ballot memorandum in this docket on another

intervenor’s appeal, in the same form: “The Commission voted to not add John M. Burrow’s

Appeal of SOAH Order No. 25 to any open meeting agenda.” 21 Oncor later cited that memorandum

in Docket No. 59315 as “indicating that the ALJs were correct in denying the motion.” 22

           If Item No. 6642 is read the same way, it could be cited as a Commission determination

that SOAH Order No. 35 was correct, or that the PBRP engineering has been reviewed and found

sound. Mr. Kennedy does not understand the October 13 vote to have made either determination.

He asks the Commission to confirm whether the PBRP engineering has been reviewed and found

sound, so that the record on Preliminary Order Issue No. 11 reflects what was and was not decided.

C.         Clarification of an unexplained ruling has been provided in this docket before.

           There have been other requests for clarifications in this docket. Using Texas Gov’t Code

2001.051(2) as authority, Intervenor Texas Scottish Rite Hospital also sought a clarification of

Order 35, the same Order at issue here, regarding whether it meant that Intervenors in 59182 would

have an equal opportunity to brief the remand issues in 59475. 23 The ALJs responded with a

clarification that 59182 Intervenors were allowed to brief the remand issues in 59475. 24

     Ballot Memorandum (June 22, 2026) (Item No. 6325 in Docket No. 59475).
22
   Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC to Amend Its Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for
the Dinosaur Switch-Longshore Switch 765-kV Transmission Line Project, Docket No. 59315, Oncor Electric
Delivery Company LLC’s Reply to Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision at 15 & n.53 (Aug. 7, 2026) (59475,
Item No. 5774).
23
     TSRH's Motion to Confirm Applicability of SOAH Order No. 35 (59182, Item No. 622)
24
     SOAH Order No. 28 (59182, Item No. 623) and SOAH Order No. 36 (59475, Item No. 6608)



KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                               Page 6 of 9
            Also, intervenor George Noelke moved for clarification of a SOAH ruling that read only,

after a summary of the parties’ arguments: “Having considered the pleadings, Mr. Noelke’s

Objection is OVERRULED and his motion is DENIED.” 25 He explained in his request for a

clarification that he could not tell whether the ruling rested on procedural, jurisdictional, or

substantive grounds, and that a party is entitled to an opportunity “to respond and to present

evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.” 26 The ALJs responded favorably to

his argument and provided the clarification. 27

           Mr. Kennedy asks the Commission for the same thing: a statement of the grounds. The

very same authority, Texas Gov’t Code 2001.051(2), used in the two examples above equally

applies in this situation.

D.         The relief requested does not require reopening the evidentiary record.

           SOAH Order No. 34 states that “[t]he evidentiary record will not be reopened.” 28

Clarification requires no evidence and no change to the remand schedule. If the Commission elects

to act on the request in Item No. 6601, the Commission “may at any time institute formal

investigations on its own motion . . . into any matter within the commission’s jurisdiction,” 29 and

PURA permits directives to ERCOT through a contested case. 30 The Commission can then decide

what effect, if any, the results should have on this proceeding.

30
     PURA § 39.1514(a)(1).



KENNEDY 59182 & 59475: Motion for Reconsideration of Ballot Memorandum                               Page 7 of 9
                                    V. RELIEF REQUESTED

Mr. Kennedy respectfully requests that the Commission:

           1. Refer ERCOT’s TEPA violation to TBPELS for investigation;

           2. Rule on the request in the Appeal (Item No. 6601) that the Commission exercise its
               authority under PURA § 39.151(d) and (d-4); OR rule that the October 13, 2026,
               vote disposed of that request and by what grounds. Explain with reasonable detail
               the grounds on which the Commission declined to place the appeal of SOAH Order
               No. 35 on an open meeting agenda, whether procedural, jurisdictional, or on the
               merits;

           3. In the alternative, rule that Item No. 6642 ballot memorandum is the notice
               provided for in 16 TAC § 22.123(a)(6) and (a)(7)(A), and is not a determination on
               the validity of ERCOT’s PBRP and 2024 RTP engineering; and

           4. Grant such other relief to which Mr. Kennedy may be entitled.



                               VI. PRESERVATION OF ERROR

       Mr. Kennedy preserves his objection to the denial of an independent technical investigation

of the PBRP, 2024 RTP and other engineering on which Applicants rely for Preliminary Order

Issue No. 11, including SOAH Order No. 35 and the October 13, 2026, Ballot Memorandum. He

will identify these rulings with particularity in any motion for rehearing of the final order, as Tex.

Gov’t Code § 2001.146(g) requires.
